sanskrit: कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् । तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
hindiTranslation: सम्पूर्ण प्राणी अन्नसे उत्पन्न होते हैं ।  अन्न वर्षासे होती है ।  वर्षा यज्ञसे होती है ।  यज्ञ कर्मोंसे निष्पन्न होता है ।  कर्मोंको तू वेदसे उत्पन्न जान और वेदको अक्षरब्रह्मसे प्रकट हुआ जान ।  इसलिये वह सर्वव्यापी परमात्मा यज्ञ कर्तव्यकर्म में नित्य प्रतिष्ठित है ॥
englishTranslation: Know that action comes from the Vedas, and the Vedas come from the imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervading supreme reality is always established in sacrifice.
essence: Right action is not random; it rests in a deeper, sustaining order.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Action arises from sacred order, that order arises from the imperishable, and the all-pervading supreme reality is rooted in selfless offering.
simpleInsight: Work feels lighter when you see it as part of a larger order, not a personal burden.
detailedMeaning: After showing how sacrifice sustains life, Krishna now traces action back to the Vedas and beyond them to the imperishable source, grounding karma yoga in cosmic order.
modernRelevance: A village head deciding where the new well goes knows the choice touches every household. Seeing it as part of a larger order, he sets aside his own family's convenience and decides for all of them.
translationLiteral: कर्म (action) / ब्रह्मोद्भवं (born from Brahman) / विद्धि (know) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / अक्षरसमुद्भवम् (arising from the imperishable) / तस्मात् (therefore) / सर्वगतम् (all-pervading) / ब्रह्म (Brahman) / नित्यम् (always) / यज्ञे (in sacrifice) / प्रतिष्ठितम् (established)
insight: Action comes from the Vedas, the Vedas from the imperishable, so Brahman abides in sacrifice.
